# Step 2, the variant that keeps part of the balance: 1,720.00 USD leave the
# bank and 1,000.00 USD stay in it, so the book ends the year holding a
# realized loss on the dollars that went and an unrealized loss on the dollars
# it still has. The reported example spends every dollar, which is why it
# cannot tell the two apart; this one can.
#
# `{usd_basis}` is the basis split `fx-balances` reports after
# `tests/fixtures/a_usd_invoice_collected_into_a_usd_bank.txt`. A guid is made
# fresh on every import, so it cannot be written into a fixture: the test reads
# it from that listing and substitutes it before importing this ledger onto
# that book.
#
# The dollars leave valued at what they cost — 189557/136000 CAD/USD, so
# 2,397.34 CAD for the 1,720.00 — while the CAD bank receives the 2,384.78 they
# fetched at 1.3865. The 12.56 between them is the realized loss, and it stands
# apart in the residual rather than being folded into either side.
#
# What stays: 1,000.00 USD, costing 1,393.80 CAD and worth 1,386.50 at the year
# end, an unrealized loss of 7.30. The two come to the 19.86 the whole balance
# loses when every dollar is spent.
#
# Measured on GnuCash 5.10, GnuCash's own Balance Sheet states 12.56 as its
# Unrealized Gains for this book — the realized loss with its sign reversed,
# already inside the 3,778.58 of retained earnings — states the 7.30 nowhere,
# and prints 3,771.28 of assets against 3,791.14 of liabilities and equity.

2026-08-17 * "Sent part of the balance out"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:Bank 2384.78 CAD
	Assets:Bank:USD -1720.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "189557/136000"
		value: "-2397.34"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
